subject: AI & Agents
title: Transfer Learning: Standing on Giant Shoulders
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Transfer Learning: Standing on Giant Shoulders.

hook.text: Train a model on a million images, then adapt it for medical scans with just 200 examples. That's transfer learning.

buildup.text: Training from scratch requires massive datasets. Transfer learning reuses knowledge from pre-trained models.

discovery.text: Early layers learn general features like edges and textures. Later layers specialize for the new task.

twist.text: Sometimes transferred knowledge hurts — if the source domain is too different, negative transfer occurs.

climax.text: Transfer learning made AI practical for fields with limited data — medicine, agriculture, rare languages.

punchline.text: Don't start from zero. Start from where someone else finished.

quiz.question: When can transfer learning be harmful?
options: When the source domain is too different from the target task
When the model is too small

details.summary: Transfer learning reuses a model trained on one task as the starting point for a different task. Instead of learning from scratch, it adapts existing knowledge, making AI practical with small datasets.
details.whyItMatters: Most organizations do not have massive datasets. Transfer learning democratizes AI by letting anyone fine-tune powerful pre-trained models for specific needs with modest data and compute.
takeaways: Pre-trained models provide learned features as a starting point
Fine-tuning adapts these features to specific new tasks
It makes powerful AI accessible with limited data and compute

faq.question: How much data is needed for transfer learning?
faq.answer: Dramatically less than training from scratch. Fine-tuning a pre-trained model can work with hundreds or thousands of examples for a new task, versus millions needed to train from scratch.

faq.question: When does transfer learning not work well?
faq.answer: When the new task is very different from the original training domain. A model trained on text will not transfer well to medical imaging. The source and target domains need some shared structure.
